text:
sam: Heads-up — customer (FinPlan) opened a Priority P1: hosted API returns 400 when calling the price_lookup tool. Also hitting our eval CI: the golden prompt for price-ranking is failing with a schema validation error. Creating this thread to collect repro steps and assign owners.

kevin: can you paste the request/response and the error payload?

sam: customer request (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/invoke
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-price-1",
  "input": "Find best price for SKU 6884",
  "tool_call": {
    "name": "price_lookup",
    "args": {
      "product_id": "6884",
      "max_price": "100"  // sent as string
    }
  }
}
```

sam: response:
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "Tool argument validation failed",
  "details": ["price_lookup.max_price: expected number, got string"]
}
```

mia: confirmed the schema for price_lookup in the tool registry expects max_price: number. Our adapter does strict JSON schema validation. This used to coerce strings -> numbers in older runtime but we tightened it in v2.

jordan: the eval CI is failing on the golden prompt because the harness simulates the same call with a golden input that currently uses a numeric max_price. But we added a new golden-case that uses string inputs to mirror incoming traffic; the test asserts the toolcall matches schema and fails when conversion isn't applied. CI output: "schema validation error at args.max_price". ci-bot posted the failing job: https://ci.redwood.internal/ops/9876 (logs attached).

ci-bot: Build #9876 failed: price_lookup-golden-case (schema validation). See /artifacts/9876/price-golden.log

alex: quick question — are customers getting charged for these failed calls? Is it a billing break?

lina: calls that fail in validation do not bill token usage on our billing pipeline (we short-circuit). But the customer sees repeated retries which increases API call counts and may trigger rate limits / chargeable retries if they wrap calls differently. We should clarify on support ticket.

kevin: root cause hypothesis: recent runtime change (strict-tool-schema flag) enforces primitive types in the tool adapter. Previously we had a best-effort coercion layer that would attempt number parsing. It was removed to reduce silent data errors. This surfaced because clients often send numbers as strings from web forms.

sam: customer repro steps I ran locally: 1) curl the endpoint with max_price as string (see above) -> 400. 2) curl with max_price as 100 (number) -> 200 and tool returns expected JSON.

sam: local curl for working case:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/invoke -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-price-1","input":"Find best price for SKU 6884","tool_call":{"name":"price_lookup","args":{"product_id":"6884","max_price":100}}}'
```

jordan: two-pronged remediation: (A) short-term customer workaround: update client to cast max_price to number before calling; (B) short-term platform mitigation: re-introduce optional coercion for a whitelist of tools (price_lookup included) behind a feature flag so we can reduce customer breakage while we improve surface area. Long-term: update eval/golden suites to include mixed-type fuzzing and tighten docs.

kevin: agree. I'd prefer platform-side safe-coercion as a toggle. We must ensure we log coercions and emit a deprecation warning header so clients can fix.

alex: for the support response: tell FinPlan to apply quick cast change and offer to toggle feature-flag on their org until they ship the client fix. Also offer to run a smoke test on their account.

mia: I'll draft a support reply. Also flagging product for docs update (tool schemas example showing numeric vs string).

jordan: CI change required: add a pre-submit smoke job that runs the failing golden-case against a local gateway with strict-tool-schema disabled and enabled to ensure we catch regressions both ways. Add a unit test for price_lookup that includes args where max_price is a string.

kevin: timeline + owners:
- kevin: implement feature-flagged coercion + logging (ETA 1 workday)
- jordan: add CI smoke + unit tests (ETA 2 workdays)
- mia: customer comms + temporary toggle request (today)
- sam: run the smoke repro on FinPlan account and confirm (today)

sam: sample patch for coercion (internal only):
```js
// pseudo
function coerceArgs(schema, args) {
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(schema.properties)) {
    if (v.type === 'number' && typeof args[k] === 'string') {
      const n = Number(args[k]);
      if (!Number.isNaN(n)) {
        args[k] = n;
        metrics.increment('tool.coercion.applied', {tool: schema.title, arg: k});
      }
    }
  }
  return args;
}
```

lina: note: if we enable coercion, check downstream tool implementations (some rely on type errors). Add a canary to Dedicated customers only first.

ci-bot: Patchset created: CL 4521 by kevin -> feature/strict-tool-coercion. CI: presubmit running.

sam: I'll attach the customer's request id to the CL and ask infra to enable the flag on FinPlan's org for now.

mia: Draft reply ready: short version — we found the issue: max_price sent as string; quick fix is to cast to number or we can flip a platform toggle temporarily. Asking customer if they'd like us to enable the toggle while they deploy the client change.

alex: also add an eval regression task: expand golden prompt corpus with a fuzz-case generator that randomly swaps primitive types for fields used in tool calls. Avoid brittle golden-only tests.

jordan: created issue: https://tracker.redwood.ai/ISSUE-2217 "fuzz mixed-type toolcall args in golden/eval suites"

sam: action items captured. I'll update this thread when CL lands and when we flip flag on FinPlan. :thumbsup:

kevin: quick note — if anyone wants to reproduce quickly: run unit harness with env TOOL_SCHEMA_COERCE=true and re-run failing golden-case.

mia: tagging @support on the ticket. Closing loop when customer accepts toggle. :eyes:
